verdict.summary: The Ni-N3 motif is reported experimentally, so it is not new. I opened the abstracts of 7 candidates. Zang et al. (Adv. Mater. 2021) describe isolated Ni with three N donors for HER, supported by XAFS and DFT. Fu et al. (Small 2022) describe isolated NiN3 sites on highly defective carbon for CO2RR. Both match the donor element and count on a carbon support. Neither abstract confirms the graphene single-vacancy geometry, and neither gives a dG_H value comparable to ours (-0.02 eV). Zhang et al. (Angew. 2025) is related only, because its Ni-N3 sites are stabilized by Ni6N6 nanoclusters. The Chem. Sci. 2021 paper computes NiNxC4-x moieties and finds NiN4 dominant, so it is related. Qiu et al. (2016) has Ni on graphene with no N donors stated, so it is related. Buonocore et al. (2019) covers Mg, Zn, Pd and Pt on N-doped vacancies, not Ni, so it is also related. The Hollow N-doped carbon spheres paper (JCIS 2023) names Ni-N3 only in its title, and its abstract gives no coordination. I did not check the remaining 3 candidates (graphene-defect trapping, Ni adatom migration, Ni-N2O2), which the task already classed as related. One caveat for novelty claims: the abstracts do not show that a vacancy-type Ni-N3 on graphene has been computed with dG_H, so only the physical motif is established as reported, not necessarily our exact dG_H calculation.

No opened abstract states a Cu atom with exactly two N and one C donors on graphene or doped carbon. The closest is Wu et al. 2024. It computes TM-N2X with X = C on graphene, but its abstract names only CuN3 and CuN2B for Cu, so a CuN2C entry is possible but unconfirmed. It treats OER/ORR, not HER. Du et al. 2023 covers N2C2 and N3C, which are different donor counts. Jovanovic 2021 covers Cu on a C3 vacancy and on N- or B-doped graphene, not N2C. The Cu/Ni carbon nitride paper is N4. The Nano Lett 2020 Cu-SA/NC paper only says N-doped carbon, with no coordination given in the abstract. The Stone-Wales HER paper has no N donors and does not name Cu. So I class this as related only, not reported. A full-text check of Wu 2024 (its Cu and X = C data and any H adsorption values) would settle whether CuN2C was computed for OER/ORR, but even then HER would stay unreported.

None describes a single Fe atom with exactly one N, two S and one O as first-shell donors on a carbon support. The S/N-coordinated Fe papers all have different donor counts: Fe-N3S1 (several papers), the FeNnS4-n series (n=1-4) and FeSxN4-x (x=1-4). The only one with an oxygen donor is the Small 2022 paper (Fe-N3S1 plus an axial OH, five-coordinate), so it is N3S1+O and not NS2O. The Sulfur-Coordinated TM/graphene NRR paper covers TM-S4 sites, which is S4 and not NS2O. The N,S-co-doped graphene oxide paper is N/S-Fe-N4, with S only in the support. The 2022 PCCP paper is Fe1/2/3 clusters on N-doped graphene for N2 reduction, not a single-atom NS2O. The extra search returned only HER papers on Fe/Ru on N-defective graphene, Co-N-C, and M4 clusters. I did not open these, so they are unchecked, though their titles do not point to NS2O. The Fe-NS2O motif therefore looks unreported in this corpus. This holds only for what the Valency index covers. Papers not indexed there, or that use other nomenclature, could still exist.
